trajectory_summary: This is a short, compliance-driven call where the customer cooperates through a rapid-fire verify sequence but never gets real engagement or a locked next step. The rep collects fragmented bill data and closes with a vague text-and-callback promise rather than a scheduled appointment, leaving the outcome open-ended.
outcome_dispute: This call should not be tagged as booked or tentative. The rep's own words — 'I'll send you a text... and then I'll call you, and then we'll schedule you' — describe a future callback with no day or time attached, which is a callback outcome, not a booking.

observed_outcome.quote: Okay. So I'll just I'll send you a text saying this is Bucky with Ion. And then Uh-huh. When you get home, you can just take a picture of that graph, send it to me, and then I'll call you, and then we'll schedule you.
observed_outcome.reasoning: The rep explicitly defers scheduling until after the customer sends a bill photo and the rep calls back — no day or time is set, so this is a callback outcome, not a booked or tentative appointment.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captures a garbled but approximate $300/month figure and responds only with 'Okay' before moving to the next verify item — the number is never confirmed, repeated back, or used as leverage later in the call.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never asks what interested the customer in solar; the call moves directly from intro into address/homeowner verification and stays in a pure data-collection mode throughout.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Unanchored close — no locked callback time
primary_coaching_focus.quote: Okay. So I'll just I'll send you a text saying this is Bucky with Ion.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The entire call funnels toward this moment, and it ends without a specific day/time or verbal handshake, leaving the lead in a soft, unaccountable state that is easy to lose. This is the single highest-leverage fix for this rep on this call.

key_moments.stewart_read: The customer's bill figure comes through as uncertain and self-corrected three times in five seconds. The rep says only 'Okay' and moves straight to the roof question without confirming the number or acknowledging the pain it represents.

key_moments.quote: We're just looking for your yearly kilowatt usage history. It's the last thing we need. It's I need 12,000 kilowatts
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep frames the bill/usage ask purely as a data requirement ('it's the last thing we need') rather than connecting it to what the customer gets out of it (a specific savings design). No curiosity is created about her own numbers.

key_moments.quote: I don't know. I need to work in the hospital right now.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer states a real logistical constraint (she's at work, possibly at a hospital job) and the rep does not acknowledge it at all before continuing with the bill-access ask. There is no schema section directly matching acknowledgment of a stated time constraint outside protocols.time_constraint (which covers the customer asking about call length, not this reverse case), so this is flagged as an ungrounded schema gap rather than forced into an ill-fitting category.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. The yeah. We're partnered with Tesla. Yes.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer directly asks if this is about Tesla solar, and the rep confirms the Tesla partnership without clarifying that Ion sells its own panels plus the Tesla Powerwall battery, not Tesla panels or roof tiles. The customer's question signals she may be expecting Tesla-branded product.
